neighbours.label: A verb reporting a change of status at some point ('when the ADA was revised', 'Oklahoma became a state', 'have survived those years'); the same subjects with a static verb stay low.
fire: Back in 1959, when Alaska became a state, few people lived there.
Since May 2014, when the code was amended, only nurses qualify.
Their old songs and recipes have vanished over those long centuries.
Nevada became a state during the war (the map shows it).
As of June 2009, when the rule was repealed, anyone may enter.
Serbia became independent long after the empire fell.
Local customs have vanished over two hundred years of rule.
In April 1998, when the law was changed, only adults could vote.
quiet: Back in the hills, where Alaska is cold, few people live.
Since May 2014, when the code was short, only nurses qualify.
Their old songs and recipes are in those long books.
Nevada has many towns (the map shows them).
In June, when the room is hot, anyone may leave.
Serbia is located far south of the old empire.
Local customs are listed in two hundred pages of notes.
In April 1998, when the park was green, only adults played golf.

short: verb reporting a change of status
notes: Probes: ' became' 0.55, ' revised' 0.45, ' have' 0.30; 'Festival' after 'recently-revived' 0.17, ' not' 0.17, 'no longer' 0.08. 'When the ADA was open' read 0.19, so a past frame leaks; two near misses keep such a frame. ' have' peaks before the verb is visible. On this pole the output direction suppresses ' now', ' today', ' modern', ' obsolete'.
